title: Supported perfect approximation on an affine scheme
statement: Let $Y$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $T\subseteq Y$ be closed, let $m\in\mathbf Z$, and let $s\ge0$ be an integer. Let $F\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-derived-category] be $m$-pseudo-coherent [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Assume that $Y\setminus T$ is a union of $s$ affine open subschemes and that $H^i(F)_y=0$ for every $i\ge m-s+1$ and every $y\notin T$. Then there exist a perfect object $P\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-perfect-complex] and a morphism $v:P\to F$ such that all cohomology stalks of $P$ outside $T$ vanish, $H^i(v)$ is an isomorphism for $i>m$, and $H^m(v)$ is surjective. In particular $\mathsf A(Y)$ holds [def-sfb-supported-perfect-approximation-property].

proof.text: Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Put $U=Y\setminus T$. An $m$-pseudo-coherent object is $a$-pseudo-coherent for every $a\ge m$: the same local approximation has isomorphisms in degrees $>a$ and a surjection at $a$. On each member of its defining cover, $F$ has zero cohomology above the maximum of $m$ and the upper bound of the strictly perfect local approximation. Since the affine scheme $Y$ is quasi-compact, finitely many such members cover $Y$; the maximum of their bounds is a global cohomological upper bound. Fix $Y,T,m,s$ and prove the conclusion for all admissible $F$ with $H^i(F)=0$ for $i>t$, by induction on $\max(0,t-m+1)$. If $t<m$, take $P=0$ and the zero map: all required target cohomology sheaves, including $H^m(F)$, vanish.

For the induction step let $t\ge m$. The preceding monotonicity makes $F$ $t$-pseudo-coherent. On the small Zariski ringed site the stated local strictly perfect definition is precisely the scheme definition. Apply the top-cohomology finite-type theorem at degree $t$ to obtain that $H^t(F)$ is finite type. It is quasi-coherent because $F\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$. The affine finite-type criterion says that $\Gamma(Y,H^t(F))$ has finitely many generators $c_1,\ldots,c_n$.

Apply the supported-class lifting lemma to $E=F[t]$ and to each $c_j\in\Gamma(Y,H^0(F[t]))$. Indeed, for $-s+1\le q\le0$ one has $t+q\ge m-s+1$, so $H^q(F[t])|_U=H^{t+q}(F)|_U=0$. It gives $a_j:K_j\to F[t]$ and a section lifting $c_j$, with $K_j$ perfect, supported on $T$, and having no positive cohomology. Set $Q=\bigoplus_{j=1}^nK_j[-t]$ and let $q:Q\to F$ be the sum of the shifted maps. Then $Q$ is perfect, supported on $T$, and $H^i(Q)=0$ for $i>t$. The image of $H^t(q)$ contains every $c_j$. These sections generate the sheaf $H^t(F)$: under the affine tilde/global-sections counit this is the sheafification of the surjection $A^n\to\Gamma(Y,H^t(F))$, and the tilde functor preserves cokernels. Thus $H^t(q)$ is surjective. The empty set of generators gives $Q=0$.

Complete $q$ to a distinguished triangle $Q\to F\to F_1\to Q[1]$. Since $Q$ is perfect, its local strictly perfect representatives show directly that it is $(m+1)$-pseudo-coherent. The triangle pseudo-coherence theorem, part (1), makes $F_1$ $m$-pseudo-coherent. The long exact cohomology sequence gives $H^i(F_1)=0$ for $i\ge t$, using the surjection at $t$ and vanishing above $t$ of $Q,F$. For $y\in U$, its stalk sequence has both adjacent cohomology stalks of $Q$ zero, hence $H^i(F)_y\cong H^i(F_1)_y$ for all $i$. Therefore the required support bound persists. Also $F_1\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$: $Q$ is a finite sum of shifts of the objects $K_j$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$, and closure of the quasi-coherent derived property under shifts and triangle middle terms, applied to $F\to F_1\to Q[1]$, gives this assertion. Apply the induction hypothesis at bound $t-1$ to obtain $v_1:P_1\to F_1$ with $P_1$ perfect supported on $T$, isomorphisms above $m$, and a surjection at $m$.

Let $d:F_1\to Q[1]$ be the connecting map. Complete $d\circ v_1$ to a triangle and rotate it to obtain a distinguished triangle $Q\to P\to P_1\xrightarrow{d\circ v_1}Q[1]$. Apply TR3 to the rotated triangles $P_1\to Q[1]\to P[1]\to P_1[1]$ and $F_1\to Q[1]\to F[1]\to F_1[1]$, with first maps $v_1$ and $1_{Q[1]}$. Shifting the resulting third map back gives $v:P\to F$ and a morphism of the original triangles whose other components are $1_Q$ and $v_1$. The two perfect outer terms $Q,P_1$ imply that $P$ is perfect. At a point outside $T$, the long exact sequence of the upper triangle has zero outer stalks in every degree, so every cohomology stalk of $P$ there is zero.

Check the cohomology comparison on stalks, with every class below understood in the stalk at an arbitrary fixed point. For $i\ge m$, a class $z\in H^i(F)$ maps to a class $z_1\in H^i(F_1)$. Lift $z_1$ through $H^i(v_1)$ to $x_1\in H^i(P_1)$. Its connecting image in $H^{i+1}(Q)$ is zero by commutativity. Exactness lifts $x_1$ to $x\in H^i(P)$; then $z-H^i(v)x$ comes from $H^i(Q)$, so adjust $x$ by this class. This proves surjectivity. If $i>m$ and $H^i(v)x=0$, injectivity of $H^i(v_1)$ shows that $x$ comes from $a\in H^i(Q)$. Its image in $H^i(F)$ is zero, so $a$ comes from some $b\in H^{i-1}(F_1)$. Since $i-1\ge m$, surjectivity of $H^{i-1}(v_1)$ lifts $b$ to $H^{i-1}(P_1)$. The upper exact sequence now says that the image of $a$ in $H^i(P)$, namely $x$, is zero. This proves injectivity for $i>m$ and completes the induction. These arguments use the long exact sequences of the triangle morphism; the cited stalk exactness makes them exact on stalks. Bijective stalk maps give sheaf isomorphisms. Surjective stalk maps make the cokernel have all stalks zero, so its map to the zero sheaf is an isomorphism by the same criterion; hence the sheaf map is an epimorphism.

Finally let $T$ have retrocompact complement. Taking the affine open $W=Y$ in its definition shows that $U=Y\setminus T$ is quasi-compact, so choose a finite affine open covering with $s$ members. In the definition of $\mathsf A(Y)$ take $r=s$. If $F$ is $(m-s)$-pseudo-coherent, the same approximations make it $m$-pseudo-coherent; its support hypothesis for degrees $i\ge m-s$ implies the hypothesis for degrees $i\ge m-s+1$ used above. The proved assertion therefore supplies all clauses of $\mathsf A(Y)$. This covers $s=0$ and the empty affine scheme as well.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q17-ebb8d2f57 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, the new node and every cited statement against Stacks perfect.tex 08EQ, 08E3, 08DD and 08EM/08EN. The item statement equals 08EQ with r=s and is unchanged. Step 1: monotonicity of pseudo-coherence, plus a global upper bound from a finite subcover, using quasi-compactness of Y. Step 2: 08FX(1) applied at degree t gives finite type, and the affine criterion gives finitely many generators. Step 3: the class lift is applied to F[t], and the window check t+q>=m-s+1 holds. Surjectivity is checked through tilde, the counit and cokernels. Step 4: 08FV(1) with Q perfect, hence (m+1)-pseudo-coherent. The long exact sequence gives H^{>=t}(F_1)=0, support is preserved, and F_1 is in D_QCoh by the supported-qcoh node with T=Y. Step 5: TR3 on the doubly rotated triangles is valid, and P is perfect by two-out-of-three and supported on T. Step 6: I redid the stalk diagram chase myself (surjectivity for i>=m, injectivity for i>m, using surjectivity at i-1) and it is correct. Step 7: retrocompactness gives the uniform r=s, and A(Y) follows. New node lem-sfb-affine-supported-class-lift is 08E3 in section form, which is equivalent on an affine scheme for E in D_QCoh. It is statement-only, self-contained, all three search kinds are recorded, and it is not a restatement of the item: it has no pseudo-coherence hypothesis and lifts a single class. It keeps the number s of affines (which bounds the cohomological dimension) separate from the number of Koszul generators (an arbitrary principal cover). That correctly avoids 08EQ's inaccurate 'T=V(f_1..f_r)' with r equal to the affine count, since an affine U need not be principal. Small cases checked: U empty (K=O_Y), T empty (c=0), Y=Spec k[x,y] with T the origin. Duplicate grep for 08E3/08DD/Koszul class: the existing nodes (08DD colimit, augmentation vanishing, 08EH, 09IR) do not state this lift. I accept all nine declared tool_uses as generic. No SGA citations. No changes.
